# What a dependency's generator writes is kept in the build cache, so a module
# cache that has no generated tree yet takes it from there instead of running
# the generator again. The shared tier of the build cache is what hands one
# machine's run to every other.

env GOFLAGS=-mod=mod
# -x reaches the generate directives through GOFLAGS, so a generator that runs
# names itself on stderr.
env GOFLAGS=$GOFLAGS' -x'

# The first build leaves the generated tree in the build cache, whether it
# ran the generator or found an earlier run's tree there already.
go build ./...
exists $GOPATH/pkg/mod/cache/generate/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go

# A module cache with no generated tree, and the same build cache.
env GOMODCACHE=$WORK/mod2
go mod download example.com/generated
! exists $WORK/mod2/cache/generate/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go

# The tree is restored from the build cache: nothing ran the generator.
go build ./...
! stderr 'gen -out lang.gen.go'
exists $WORK/mod2/cache/generate/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go
cmp $WORK/mod2/cache/generate/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go $GOPATH/pkg/mod/cache/generate/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go

-- go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.16

require example.com/generated v1.0.0
-- use.go --
package use

import "example.com/generated/lang"

var Name = lang.Name()
